text:
marta: heads up — prod prometheus ingestion up ~38% last 4h, heatmap shows spikes on per-device gpu_util_* and nvml_temp_* series. cost alarm triggered.
ben: ugh, yep saw that alert. any recent rollout?
priya: we rolled the latest gpu-agent yesterday that added per-process GPU metrics at 100ms by default. suspected culprit.
carla: confirmed — the agent now exports per-process per-gpu labels (pid, process_name) which exploded cardinality.
ben: short term: can we relabel/remove those labels in scrape config? example: 

```
- job_name: 'gpu-agents'
  static_configs:
  - targets: ['10.0.1.23:9100']
  relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [process_name]
    action: replace
    regex: " .* "
    replacement: "<redacted>"
  - source_labels: [pid]
    action: drop
    regex: .+
```

carla: yeah that would mask them at scrape time. but ideally we gate high-card labels behind a feature flag in the agent so only canaries emit them.
priya: can we instead reduce scrape frequency for the per-process metrics to 30s or 60s? that would at least reduce ingestion while we fix labeling.
marta: agree — two parallel steps: 1) prom relabel to drop pid/process_name, 2) short canary rollback of the agent flag. can infra-bot trigger canary? @infra-bot
infra-bot: starting canary rollout for gpu-agent v1.7.3 -> 3 nodes (zone-a). monitoring for 30m.
sre-oncall: please also adjust alerting thresholds — current alert fires on rate increases without a noise window. add a 10m for sustained ingestion before paging.
ben: adding a grafana panel for series cardinality by job and a dashboard row for per-device token cost. will patch the SLO dashboard.
carla: quick snippet for agent config to make per-process optional: 

```
gpu_agent:
  metrics:
    per_process: false
    per_device_interval_ms: 1000
```

priya: I'll open a PR to default per_process:false and add a migration note.
marta: timeline?
priya: PR in 30m, canary rollback now, full roll back if canary shows >5x ingestion.
ben: once relabels are live, I'll run a prometheus TSDB compaction plan and lower retention for the affected tsdb blocks to cut cost temporarily.
sre-oncall: +1 on retention tweak but coordinate on runbook.
marta: thanks all. follow-up: 2061202400 — infra-bot posted canary health, looks ok so far. will update after 30m. :thumbsup:
